_meta.purpose: The named deliverable that proves eval/compare.py is trustworthy. Each case is a (gold_result, candidate_result, expected_verdict) triple the comparator must reproduce. This file holds the Issue-11 baseline (the trivial rules: exact value equality and the distinct empty-result case). The subtle rules — order-sensitivity gated on ORDER BY, NULL/float/column canonicalization, multiset semantics, BIRD alignment — get their own fixture files in Issues 12-14.
_meta.format: Each case: {id, description, gold_sql, gold_result:{columns,rows}, candidate_result:{columns,rows}, expected_verdict} where expected_verdict is 'correct' | 'incorrect'. Optional 'rules' (list of canonicalization-rule names) overrides eval.compare.DEFAULT_RULES for that case. Adding a case here is exercised automatically by tests/test_compare.py.
_meta.rule: Comparison is on result-set VALUES, never the SQL string and (in this slice) not the column labels — a correct value under a different alias is still correct (CLAUDE.md domain rule 1).

cases.description: Same values in the same order → correct.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM users WHERE country = 'US';

cases.description: A plainly wrong scalar value → incorrect.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM users WHERE country = 'US';

cases.description: Same value under a different column label is still correct — comparison is on values, not column names (CLAUDE.md domain rule 1).
cases.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM users WHERE country = 'US';

cases.description: Multi-row result, identical rows in identical order → correct.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM merchants WHERE category = 'software' ORDER BY name;

cases.description: Candidate drops a row the gold has → incorrect.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM merchants WHERE category = 'software' ORDER BY name;

cases.description: Two empty result sets → correct. Empty is a distinct, correct-able case (a legitimately empty answer), not an error.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT id FROM users WHERE country = 'ZZ';

cases.description: Empty gold vs a non-empty candidate → incorrect. Empty is never auto-correct; it must match.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT id FROM users WHERE country = 'ZZ';

cases.description: Non-empty gold vs an empty candidate → incorrect (the symmetric case).
cases.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM users WHERE country = 'US';
